note: Recast from the description of the new species by Rocha & Cancello (2009), original in English; the specific epithet mirim comes from the Tupi language and means “small”, referring to the body size of the soldier; no measurement data.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is distinguished from the other species of the genus by the combination of small fontanelle and small compound eyes; the most similar species is O. okeyma, from which it differs in the labral setae arranged in two rows. The soldier has type-1 mandibles and the smallest head capsule among the species of this type, and a labrum without lateral lobes, which distinguishes it from all other species of the genus; the most similar species is O. pilosus, whose soldier has denser short hairs on the head capsule.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes small, separated from the lower margin of the head by a distance equal to the greatest diameter of an ocellus. Ocelli kidney-shaped and narrow in dorsal view; oval in lateral view, separated from the compound eye by its least diameter. Fontanelle narrow and small. Head capsule with short hairs and scattered setae. Labral setae arranged in two rows. Pronotum with short hairs and scattered setae, mainly along the margins; mesonotum and metanotum with short hairs, concentrated on the apex and the posterior margin. Head and pronotum dark brown, tergites brown to pale brown, sternites pale brown to yellow, legs brown to pale brown, wing scales dark brown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sides of the head parallel in dorsal view. Dorsal tubercle slightly prominent in lateral view, situated between the two lateral projections. Mandibles type 1, with a tooth-like process on the proximal half. Head capsule sparsely setose, the short hairs variable from sparse over the whole head capsule to denser only apically; minute hairs scattered over all surfaces. Postmentum with setae and short hairs. Surface of the pronotum with setae and short hairs, denser on the margins; posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum with setae and short hairs; abdominal tergites densely covered with short hairs and setae, the sternites with short hairs and erect setae on the posterior margin.
